staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced the saved AddressSanitizer double-free against this preserved vulnerable checkout. The patch in `dataset/arvo/19208/patch.diff` adds a duplicate-object-ID rejection in `coolkey_add_object()`, matching the source-level lifetime flaw described here.

classification.classification_note: The fuzzed reader feeds attacker-controlled APDU reply chunks into the CoolKey emulator. During initialization, attacker-controlled object metadata is materialized into `object_id` values and `coolkey_add_object()` can be reached from both the combined-object parser and the outer object-list walk. The vulnerable `coolkey_add_object()` does not enforce uniqueness, so duplicate IDs can coexist in `priv->objects_list` regardless of which admission pair produced the duplicate. Later, `coolkey_fill_object()` looks objects up by ID and caches the newly malloc'd buffer into the first matching list entry while also storing that same pointer in the currently iterated duplicate entry. Cleanup then iterates the whole list and frees both aliases, producing the witnessed heap double-free in `coolkey_free_private_data()`.

bug_description.normalized: The staged fuzz harness models card communication by slicing the testcase into 16-bit-length-prefixed response chunks. On the witnessed path, one of those chunks is consumed by `fuzz_reader_transmit()` as an APDU response for the CoolKey object-list / object-read sequence, and `sc_pkcs15_bind()` accepts the resulting simulated card as a CoolKey token. During `coolkey_initialize()`, attacker-controlled object IDs are materialized both from the combined-object parser and from the outer object-list walk, and each such path can call `coolkey_add_object()`. In the vulnerable source `coolkey_add_object()` appends every object without checking whether `object_id` is already present, so duplicate IDs can coexist in `priv->objects_list` without the saved artifacts proving which admission pair created the crashing duplicate. Later, template lookup over that list reaches a duplicate whose `data` field is still NULL, causing `coolkey_fill_object()` to allocate a fresh buffer for that object's contents. Instead of binding that buffer only to the current list element, `coolkey_fill_object()` re-finds the object by ID and stores the same `new_obj_data` into the first matching entry as well as into the current duplicate entry. `coolkey_free_private_data()` finally walks the list and frees `o->data` for every element, so both aliases of the same heap pointer are freed and AddressSanitizer reports the saved double-free at `card-coolkey.c:819`. The staged patch fixes the common lifetime obligation by rejecting duplicate IDs up front in `coolkey_add_object()`.

source.description: First non-harness project statement that consumes testcase bytes into the response-chunk state later served as synthetic APDU replies. This length/value pair determines the card responses from which CoolKey initialization reads object metadata.
source.value_from: The exact witness is the staged testcase at `gt_results/arvo_19208/poc`, which Stage 01 ran under `fuzz_pkcs15_reader`. `fuzz_get_chunk()` is the first statement below the fuzzer entry that reads those bytes into vulnerability-relevant chunk state used by later reader responses.

sink.description: Crash sink. Cleanup iterates every object list entry and frees its cached `data` pointer independently; once duplicate entries share the same heap buffer, the later iteration frees the already-freed pointer and matches the saved ASan double-free.

root_cause.description: Root cause. Vulnerable `coolkey_add_object()` appends a new object record without checking whether the same `object_id` is already present in `priv->objects_list`. The patch adds `coolkey_find_object_by_id(&priv->objects_list, object_id) != NULL` here to reject that duplicate-ID state before it can create aliased ownership.

tainted_value_origin.description: The testcase controls the sequence of synthetic reader chunks that become APDU responses. Those responses determine which CoolKey objects are listed and parsed, including the duplicate `object_id` state that later produces aliased `data` ownership.

parser_admitted.description: Sample-specific APDU gate. The crashing testcase must provide a fuzz chunk with at least two bytes so the harness accepts it as a card response, assigns SW1/SW2, and exposes the remaining bytes to OpenSC as APDU payload instead of forcing the default `0x6D00` error reply.

evidence_limitations: Stage 02 is source-grounded and uses only the saved vulnerable reproduction artifacts. It did not rerun the testcase or dynamically identify the exact duplicate object ID value carried by the witness.

The patch shows that duplicate IDs were the missing obligation, but the saved sanitizer and reproduction artifacts do not identify which `coolkey_add_object()` admission pair created the crashing duplicate. Stage 02 therefore keeps duplicate provenance branch-agnostic across the combined-object and outer list-admission paths.

coarse_trace.summary: The testcase is sliced into length-prefixed reader chunks that the fuzz reader later returns as synthetic APDU responses.
CoolKey initialization accepts the fuzzed replies, processes the combined object and listed objects, and appends object records into `priv->objects_list`.
Later attribute lookup loads one duplicate object's contents, but `coolkey_fill_object()` stores the same heap buffer into both the current duplicate entry and the first list entry with that ID.
Card teardown walks the list and frees each cached `data` pointer, so the aliased buffer is freed twice and AddressSanitizer reports a double-free.

fine_trace.note: Source. The testcase's next two bytes are interpreted as the chunk length, establishing which subsequent bytes become one synthetic reader response delivered to OpenSC.
The admitted fuzz chunk is copied into the APDU response buffer, so later CoolKey parsing consumes attacker-controlled object-list and object-body bytes from this response stream.
During the outer object-list walk, CoolKey initialization materializes an attacker-controlled `object_id` from listed object metadata for one candidate list entry.
The combined-object parser can also materialize an attacker-controlled `object_id` for an embedded object that is admitted into the same list.

Root cause. Each admission path appends its object into `priv->objects_list` with no duplicate-ID check, so the list can contain at least two entries with the same `object_id` without the saved artifacts proving which path supplied the first versus second admission.

When later code needs attributes from one duplicate entry whose `data` is still NULL, `coolkey_fill_object()` allocates one heap buffer for that object's contents. ASan reports the crashing pointer was allocated in this function.

Instead of binding ownership only to the current duplicate element, the function re-finds the first list entry with that ID, then stores the same `new_obj_data` into both `obj_entry->data` and the current `obj->data`. Two list nodes now alias one heap allocation.
During card disconnect, teardown enters `coolkey_free_private_data()` and will free each list entry's cached object buffer independently.

The vulnerable code has no pre-insertion uniqueness guard here. The patch adds `coolkey_find_object_by_id(&priv->objects_list, object_id) != NULL` at this site; in the vulnerable build that guard is absent, so duplicate admissions are not blocked.
The fuzz harness accepts the current chunk as a valid APDU reply only on this branch; otherwise it synthesizes `0x6D00` with no payload and the later CoolKey object parsing path is not reached.

Sink. The cleanup loop frees the aliased pointer once for the first matching list entry and again when it reaches the duplicate entry that still holds the same `new_obj_data`, producing the saved double-free at this line.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch is source-consistent with this trace because it rejects duplicate `object_id` values before list insertion in `coolkey_add_object()`, removing the duplicate-entry state that let `coolkey_fill_object()` create aliased ownership. Stage 02 did not execute the fixed build, so it does not claim dynamic confirmation.
sanitizer_ground_truth.source: staged sanitizer_trace.txt, default_crash_trace.txt, reproduction_report.json, exact staged vulnerable source, and dataset/arvo/19208/patch.diff

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: ASan shows the crashing pointer was allocated in `coolkey_fill_object()` and freed twice in `coolkey_free_private_data()`. The patch removes the prerequisite duplicate-ID list state in `coolkey_add_object()`, which is the common source-level condition that lets one `new_obj_data` pointer become owned by two list entries regardless of which admission path created the duplicate.

format.name: Length-prefixed synthetic smart-card response stream
format.contract: The verified trigger is only the exact staged witness at `gt_results/arvo_19208/poc`. Source-grounded evidence proves this narrow contract: the testcase must provide APDU reply chunks that the fuzz reader accepts (`chunk_size >= 2`), that drive `sc_pkcs15_bind()` into the CoolKey emulator, and that cause `coolkey_initialize()` to admit at least two list entries with the same `object_id` through its vulnerable object-admission paths; later attribute lookup then loads one duplicate through `coolkey_fill_object()` and teardown frees the shared `data` pointer twice.
